cause_quote: The PostgreSQL port of the transcript readers added jsonPathValue as `sql`(${value}::jsonb #>> ${objectPath(path)})`` and used it throughout the model-context projection, so any stored event with an escaped lone surrogate or NUL fails the jsonb cast (22P02).
user_saw: On a PostgreSQL-backed Gateway, every follow-up turn in a session whose transcript held a lone surrogate escape failed with 'invalid input syntax for type json', and a user message containing NUL was dropped.
summary: Routes all PostgreSQL transcript and session-context reads through the jsonNativeFieldsValid (pg_input_is_valid jsonb) guard, decoding rejected rows in JavaScript, and replaces NUL with a space in the full-text index text.
reasoning: SQLite always accepted these escapes; the failure exists only on the PostgreSQL engine, whose transcript readers were made portable in #171545 by casting stored JSON text to jsonb (jsonPathValue, jsonArrayElements, jsonSetPath in json-values.ts plus the model-context projection), so the defect shipped with that port rather than being broken later. The later guard from #183560 covered only some readers; the FTS NUL failure belongs to the same port series, so confidence is medium on the single cause commit.
